original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Finish the length-22 seven-label split census that research/f7-l22-union-census (#3818) left capped. The five capped splits (10,9), (10,10), (11,9), (11,10), (11,11), and the two 17-point splits (11,6), (10,7) that #3708 removed only by importing #2773/#2870, are run with the unchanged merged union-budget engine on a 251-entry prefix-free cover (the 203 depth-six restricted-growth prefixes, with 012345 replaced by its 49 depth-eight extensions), with no node cap. A split is a finite exclusion only if all 251 shards exit complete with zero hits. A small-domain partition control compares sharded and unsharded hit sets where universal words exist.
scope_change_reason: The card asks which census exclusions are sound and which bounded repair is justified. #3818 already ported a proved, mutant-tested prune into the corrected engine and left an explicit resource-limited open question (OQ1): five length-22 splits capped. The named decision is f(7) in {22, 24} inside PR943's prefix-walk model (#2973). This package changes no pruning rule; it only removes the cap by finer sharding and records the receipts.
bottleneck_link: Side result in the word-census line. It settles the length-22 question that #2973, #3708, #3731 and #3818 left open, inside the stated finite model. It changes no supplier, tariff, kappa or selected record.
stop_rule: Stop after each target split has been run on all 251 cover shards or the session budget is exhausted. Any hit word is reported verbatim and the exclusion withdrawn. A split with any incomplete shard is not an exclusion.
evidence: RESULT.json: all seven target splits complete on all 251 cover shards with zero hits ((11,11) 55,385,607,437 nodes; (11,10) 52,957,641,635; (10,10) 44,378,511,529; (11,9) 14,058,107,415; (10,9) 7,027,617,655; (10,7) 700,909; (11,6) 2,247). With #3731/#3818's four exclusions they close all eleven rows of #3708's length-22 table, so no restored universal length-22 seven-label word exists in PR943's prefix-walk model, and with #2973's bounds f(7) = 24 in that model. verify.py checks the engine pin, the cover partition, the receipt and the domain closure, runs a sharded-versus-unsharded control on small domains with real universal words, and replays registered cover slices with exact per-shard node equality.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a separately implemented census (for example #3005's C++ engine) reproduce the seven length-22 split exclusions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The f(7) = 24 conclusion in the prefix-walk model rests on one C engine and its written pruning proofs.
open_questions.first_step: Lift #3005's L <= 20 gate to 22, run (10,9) on the same 251-entry cover, and compare zero-hit completion shard by shard.
open_questions.blocked_by: The #3005 engine's throughput at length 22 is unmeasured; the largest splits need about 5e10 nodes each.

open_questions.question: Can verify.py re-derive #3708's eleven-row length-22 domain from the four necessary conditions instead of taking the table as given?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would make the domain-closure check self-contained.
open_questions.first_step: Port #3708's arithmetic checks (time bound, odd budget, even budget, pair identity) into verify.py and compare the row set.
